rejections.reason: The substantive allegation is source-supported, but its object-role binding is not: the respondents-landlords are assigned RECIPIENT even though the source identifies them as the landlords whose written consent allegedly was not obtained, not as recipients of the sub-letting, assignment, or possession. The general allegation in this segment does not identify a transfer recipient.

omissions: IK-1859043:L52 supplies additional task-relevant witness evidence that the rent-note was executed in Harnam Dass's presence, that its contents were read over to his wife and she admitted them as correct, and that the tenancy terms were settled in his presence. This speaker- and stage-specific evidence bearing on acceptance of Ex. A-7 is not separately represented.

IK-1859043:L49 states that the Additional Rent Controller also held that the tenancy stood validly determined. That lower-court finding is not separately represented even though the proposal includes the competing indefinite-contractual-tenancy and statutory-tenancy positions in n4, f14, and f15.
limits: The supplied case material ends at the second-appeal court's issue framing and expressly excludes the target statutory interpretation and withheld historical final outcome, so the unresolved written-consent and tenancy-duration questions cannot be converted into target findings.
The supplied statutory reproductions expressly leave historical-version applicability unverified where stated; no missing historical consolidation can be inferred.

The supplied material does not state the Delhi Rent Control Act commencement date and does not supply a section 17 notice fact, so post-commencement and notice-dependent propositions remain limited to the uncertainty already visible in the supplied record.
